text:
anya_m: quick summary from today's bring-up for rwl-8b-v1 (int4) — dumping the headline numbers + a couple oddities. pinging @samir_k and @devon for econ/quant recs :chart_with_upwards_trend:

anya_m: results (canary traffic = 5k requests, seq=512 avg)
- int4 (q4f) vs fp16 baseline:
  - token cost: 0.28x (i.e. ~3.6x cheaper)
  - median p95 latency: +10ms / +35ms respectively (median +10ms)
  - NLU F1 (prod eval set): 82.2 -> 80.4 (delta -1.8)
  - hallucination/BC rate: 2.1% -> 2.6% (delta +0.5)
  - extreme tail: ~0.2% requests with >2x token generation vs baseline (investigating)

anya_m: aside — long-context (2k) shows bigger quality drop (~-3.2 F1) and KV-cache blowups in a few runs. attached run id: rwl-8b-int4-canary-2026-03-20

samir_k: nice, thanks. quick econ breakdown per 1M user tokens (Seattle region):
- fp16 baseline: $72.40 / 1M tokens
- int4 (q4f): $20.10 / 1M tokens
- delta = $52.3 saved / 1M tokens (~72% cost reduction)

samir_k: recommendation: route low-risk, short-turn prompts to int4 by default (e.g., embeddings, autocompete), keep high-precision flows (summarization, extractive NLU) on fp16 or int8, and implement a smart fallback if score/confidence drops. :thumbsup:

devon: on the quant side — a few notes from the bring-up bench: 
- int4 model uses per-channel quant + 4-bit group size 128. most layers fine, but attention softmax quant noise on long context causes gradual drift (explains long-context F1 drop).
- tried int4+kv-cache-preserve (cache stored in fp16) — reduces hallucinations by ~0.2% but increases median latency +6ms.
- code snippet we used to toggle kv-preserve in runtime:
```
--serve-config:
  quant_profile: q4f
  kv_cache_mode: preserve_fp16
  batcher: adaptive
```

devon: technical reco: enable int4 for short seqs (<768) with kv-preserve disabled, enable kv-preserve for mid seqs (768-1536) but route long seqs (>1536) to int8/fp16. Add a short canary for 1% production for 48h and monitor F1 + hallucination + tail latencies.

ci-bot: test-run rwl-8b-int4-canary-2026-03-20 results attached:
- total_runs: 5120
- fail_rate: 0.6% (timeoutexceptions on 9 runs)
- mean_gen_tokens: 142
- outlier_ids: ["r-112233", "r-112498", "r-112799"]

ci-bot: sample log for outlier r-112799:
```
2026-03-20T14:03:12Z ERROR generate_loop.py: timeout while processing seq>1800, kv-cache memory spike -> fallback to fp16 succeeded
```
gtm-liaison: product note — if we proceed with the route strategy, marketing/GTN needs a crisp messaging: "~3.6x cheaper for short form interactions, slight quality tradeoffs on complex long-form tasks". also need a gating doc for enterprise customers who require deterministic quality.

gtm-liaison: propose: feature flag + doc + opt-in alpha for customers to try int4 with clear SLA exceptions.

anya_m: proposed rollout plan (short):
1) Canary 1% prod for 48h (short seq only) + regen eval hooks (F1, hallucination)
2) If metrics within thresholds (F1 delta < -1.5, hallucination delta < +0.8%), expand to 10% for 7d.
3) Implement runtime routing policy: short->int4, mid->int4+kv-preserve, long->int8/fp16 fallback.
4) Add unit-econ dashboard card and alert if cost savings drop below expected band.

anya_m: action items: @samir_k to draft econ promo language, @devon to add kv-preserve flag + canary config, @gtm-liaison to draft customer opt-in doc. I'll run the 48h canary tomorrow morning and post results.

samir_k: acked. will do econ blurb and quick slide for leadership.

devon: adding canary config to infra repo, will ping when deployed.

anya_m: thanks all. brief follow-up check-in Friday or earlier if canary trips :warning:
